subject: Performance MAP: benchmarking scope, SLOs, and initial results (FlutterHealth)
messages:
From: Sonia Patel <sonia@flutterhealth.com>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP / perf bench scope request

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo today. As discussed, we need a MAP-style performance evaluation so our infra team can validate latency and throughput for the clinical-assist features. High-level asks: TTFT, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput at target concurrencies, and a short report we can share with procurement.

We can provide a synthetic prompt set and a sample production prompt trace. Can you propose a scoped plan (workload mix, SLOs, success criteria, and an estimated timeline to run baseline + tuned runs)?

Cheers,
Sonia
Sr. Platform Ops, FlutterHealth

-----
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@flutterhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP / perf bench scope request

Hi Sonia —

Appreciate the clear ask. I attached a draft MAP (MAP-draft-FlutterHealth-20260727.docx) — summary below. This is scoped to give you an apples-to-apples baseline on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (if you want an on-prem run we can add that).

Summary of proposed bench plan (short):
- Workload mix: 60% short prompts (<64 tokens), 30% mid (64–512), 10% long (>512). We will replay a 2k-sample production trace you provide and supplement with synthetic edge cases.
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 16, 24, 32 concurrent clients; steady-state runs for 10 minutes per concurrency point after warmup.
- Metrics: TTFT (time-to-first-token), p50/p95/p99 generation latencies, tokens/sec throughput, tokens-per-second-per-GPU, error rate (5xx/timeout), and cost proxy (tokens * unit-price).
- Target SLOs / success criteria (initial):
  * TTFT: p95 <= 350 ms on Dedicated; p95 <= 600 ms on Hosted
  * Latency: p95 per-response <= 1.2 s (short prompts); p99 < 2.5 s overall
  * Throughput: baseline model should sustain >= 1,000 tokens/sec at 16 concurrency on Dedicated
  * Stability: error rate < 0.5% under sustained load
- Deliverables: annotated benchmark CSV + charts, short executive summary PDF, and config files.

Questions / ask from you:
1) Can you share a 2k-sample trace (we'll redact PHI) or confirm we should use our synthetic set?
2) Any hard constraints on cost-per-token or a performance tier you want Guaranteed?

If that scope looks fine I'll schedule the runs for this week and loop in infra.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai

-----
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, Sonia Patel <sonia@flutterhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2026 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance MAP: benchmarking scope, SLOs, and initial results (FlutterHealth)

Adding a few technical specifics that will appear in the MAP draft and test config:
- Test harness: we will use Redwood's perf agent (k6-based wrapper) and our token-level tracer that records TTFT and per-token emission times. Warmup phase is 3 minutes, then 10-minute steady-state windows.
- Model variants tested: open-arch-v2-8b (quantized), rwx-7b-dedicated, and hosted-rwx-small for baseline.
- Input truncation policy: for long prompts we will run both full and truncated (512) to estimate tail behavior.
- Cost proxy: we'll show unit-cost at current public pricing and a projected cost for 1M daily tokens.
- Concurrency shaping: both constant concurrency and Poisson arrival for a subset to mimic burstiness.

Bench target numbers (for planning) — initial hypotheses to validate:
- Dedicated: TTFT p95 ~= 220–320 ms; p95 response latencies for short prompts < 220 ms; throughput > 1,200 tok/s at conc=16; scales ~1.6x from 8->16, flattens after ~24.
- Hosted (multi-tenant): TTFT p95 ~= 380–650 ms; expect higher variance and occasional spikes during background maintenance windows.

I'll provision the test runs and aim to produce a first-pass results summary in 48 hours after you share the trace.

-rishi
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Camila/Rishi — we uploaded the 2k anonymized trace to the Drive link you requested and attached a small tokenized sample set (test-workload-samples.zip). We are OK with the SLO targets you proposed; procurement would prefer a documented TTFT p95 <= 400 ms for production SLA.

Please run the baseline on Hosted and Dedicated. If the baseline fails the TTFT p95 <= 400 ms target on Dedicated we will need an executive review before we proceed to procurement. Can you confirm you can hit that window?

Sonia

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@flutterhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance MAP: benchmarking scope, SLOs, and initial results (FlutterHealth)

Sonia — quick update with the first-pass results attached (benchmark-results-20260730-summary.pdf). Top-line:

- Baseline (hosted-rwx-small): TTFT p95 = 480 ms, p95 response latency (short prompts) = 620 ms, tokens/sec @ conc=16 = 680 tok/s, error rate = 0.4%.
- Dedicated (rwx-7b-dedicated): TTFT p95 = 240 ms, p95 response latency (short prompts) = 180 ms, tokens/sec @ conc=16 = 1,260 tok/s, error rate = 0.15%.
- Concurrency behavior: Dedicated scales near-linearly 1->16, plateaus ~24 conc where per-GPU kernel saturation causes <5% throughput gains beyond 24.

Interpretation and recommended next steps:
1) Dedicated comfortably meets your procurement TTFT p95 <= 400 ms requirement and our internal success criteria.
2) Hosted baseline misses the procurement target — expected for multi-tenant tiers.
3) To reduce p95 further on Dedicated we recommend: enabling prefix KV cache for steady-state chat flows (should drop TTFT p95 by ~20%), and testing 4-bit quantized kernels for throughput gains (bench after cache).

Proposed schedule:
- Week of Aug 2: KV cache + quantization test runs (2 days), final report update (1 day).
- Week of Aug 9: Optional on-prem run (if you confirm access) and executive summary delivery to procurement.

I've included the CSV and charts in the attached PDF, and the MAP draft doc in Drive. Looping procurement if you'd like to lock the Dedicated SKUs and monthly commit after the Aug 9 confirmation.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai
